_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. Provenance: project_abnormal_print_gotchas.md (first print 2026-06-06, press 4.22.0). NOTE the big trap: a mid-build `generate --force` re-emits novel TODO stubs over implemented hand-authored novel files even without the generated header - do ALL spec repairs BEFORE implementing novels on any reprint.

handfixes.summary: Spec resources renamed to avoid reserved/collision: /search* -> email-search, /resources* -> api-resources (typed FTS table collided with framework resources_fts)
handfixes.why: `search` is a reserved template command (parse-time collision); `resources` collides with the framework `resources_fts` typed-FTS table - NOT caught at parse time, surfaces as store test failures ('no column named description') and silently-wrong runtime FTS. The renames produce the email-search / api-resources commands and typed store tables. A reprint without the x-pp-resource renames reintroduces the collisions.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: These ARE spec-encoded (x-pp-resource on the affected paths in the abnormal spec); the markers below assert the rename survived into the generated CLI + store schema. Keep the x-pp-resource annotations on any spec re-copy.

handfixes.summary: ABNORMAL_BASE_URL (EU host override) is documented in guide.md env table + troubleshoots; the press omits the optional base-URL var from docs
handfixes.why: config.go reads ABNORMAL_BASE_URL as an optional override for EU tenants (https://eu.api.abnormalplatform.com/v1); the press doc generator only documents the bearer token (ABNORMAL_API_TOKEN). Without the override documented, EU customers get empty results / 4xx with no guidance. A reprint drops the EU-host documentation.

handfixes.summary: Vendor portal URL prose must not carry the markdown-quote trailing backtick harvested from spec prose (integrations`)
handfixes.why: The vendor spec prose put a markdown backtick after 'integrations', which the press harvested verbatim into helpers/auth/doctor/mcp-tools output (a runtime artifact, not just docs). Stripped during onboarding. A reprint re-harvests the trailing backtick.

handfixes.summary: manifest.json env-var description must use prose, not the literal portal URL (its /home/settings path trips the ci_guards personal-path guard)
handfixes.why: The vendor portal URL https://portal.abnormalsecurity.com/home/settings/integrations contains a /home/<word>/ segment that ci_guards' personal-filesystem-path guard false-flags as a hardcoded /home path. Original onboard de-pathed it to prose; a re-vendor re-introduces the URL.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For abnormal the manifest gained: ABNORMAL_BASE_URL. server.json gained: ABNORMAL_BASE_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: ABNORMAL_BASE_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The learn journal minimizes what it keeps: the <PREFIX>_LEARN_SESSION override is stored as "o:" plus the 64-bit SHA-256 hash the harness session ids get; argv_shape records only flag names the invoked command declares under exactly the typed name, every other name as the "<undeclared>" placeholder, and nothing after "--"; failed_flag is never kept as typed (the placeholder plus the typed name's hash when Cobra suggested a declared flag, else nothing); teach.log records argument counts, never the arguments. Every line that reaches the journal, teach.log, the learnings audit, feedback.jsonl, profiles.json or the learn store passes the credential kit's file and SQL sinks.
handfixes.why: A credential typed where a flag goes, or set as a session label, is not a value the kit has held, so the structural rules must keep it out on their own. The connector's own RefuseHeld checks on each store are replaced by the kit's sinks (credkit-wiring, credkit-sqlite-every-handle). internal/learn/journal_credential_hardening_test.go drives every path, unheld and then held by the kit in a child process.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: learn/journal.go.tmpl should hash the LEARN_SESSION override as it hashes harness ids, and JournalArgvShape should take the invoked command's declared-flag lookup and record any other name as a placeholder, stopping at "--"; the failed flag should be an opaque identity; teach.log should not echo raw arguments; and every template that stores operator-named text should refuse one that repeats a held credential.

handfixes.summary: export --output closes its output file on every return, including an API error: the open no longer shadows RunE's named err, and the file is written through the credential kit's writer.
handfixes.why: The generated `f, err := openExportOutput(...)` inside the --output block declared a new err, so the deferred close tested that inner (nil) err and never ran when the export returned an API error. With the output chokepoint the file is a filter pipe, and the unclosed pipe kept the process from exiting: `export clients --output f.jsonl` after a 401 hung (TestExportOutputReturnsAfterAnAPIError, seen failing 3 of 4 runs). Fleet note: every connector that took the ported chokepoint edit on export.go carries the same shadowing. Ported to abnormal from the gradient 4.34.2 reprint (one credential layer across the fleet). Ported to abnormal from the liongard 4.34.2 reprint (one credential layer across the fleet).

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand and replaces this connector's own credential layer. internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one Declarations literal; each main starts with credkit.Start and ends with credkit.Exit, and every early exit of the MCP main returns through it; the API client (client.OutboundGuard), feedback, deliver and probe clients go through credkit.Transport, under the origin pin; every file write outside the 0600 credential store and config goes through the kit (cache, export, deliver, feedback, journal, teach logs, profiles, platform files); the MCP stdio and HTTP servers pass credkit.MCPIn, MCPOut, MCPHTTP and MCPTools; the MCP mirror runs the CLI with credkit.RunCommand. The store and config rewrites go outside the kit (cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile) as declared credential sources. A config or credential file is held with credkit.HoldBody and credkit.HoldURL every time it is read, and the MCP server's --tls-key file is held at startup.
handfixes.why: One contract, one matcher and one set of sinks replace the connector-only copies, and a matcher fix reaches this connector by vendoring. It closes the open review classes: a credential split across two exported records (the export is one kit stream), a short credential in a decoded view, doctor's credentials verdict (no name-based redaction), the env-schema gate (no os.Environ holder), and the MCP HTTP no-token refusal printed before os.Exit (credkit.Exit drains it). Tests: internal/credwire/leak_test.go, on the built binaries, seen failing on the pre-kit HEAD or with the wiring disabled (.review/seen/). handfixes.summary: credkit.MCPHTTP writes every response the MCP HTTP server serves, refusals included. requireBearerAuthWithLimits runs a preflight that writes nothing, then credkit.MCPHTTP around a gate that answers the Origin, bearer and body-limit verdicts.

handfixes.summary: --stdin is a declared StdinFlag, so the kit holds a body whole and line by line before anything prints. cliutil.CompactStdinBody puts a JSON body on one line first, because a line of { alone collides with public text and refuses the start. feedback --stdin refuses instead of reporting a record the kit would withhold.
handfixes.why: A request body may carry a credential, and a held body is the kit's to judge. The cost is recorded in the docs: a preview of a --stdin body, and a vendor answer repeating part of it, are withheld, and the write still happens.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate StdinFlags and the compaction with the kit wiring.

handfixes.summary: credentialFiles returns the config the program really uses first, because the kit takes the base URL and every allowed origin from the first file naming one: an explicit --config or ABNORMAL_CONFIG wins, the last --home decides the default paths, and every other file any flag could mean is only held. The credential stores are only held too: the store's base_url records where a token was issued, and config.Load takes no base URL from it. Startup reads --config and --home by their last occurrence; the root pre-run refuses a run whose parsed values differ (another flag swallowed one). abnormal-mcp, which has no such flags, refuses to start when startup read one.
handfixes.why: A discovered default's or a store's base_url must not become an allowed origin for a credential from another file.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the file discovery in the wiring file.

handfixes.summary: agent-context prints the CLI's own config, data, state and cache directories through agentContextPath (internal/cli/abnormal_agent_paths.go): forward slashes on Windows, unchanged elsewhere.
handfixes.why: CI windows row on PR #554: a Windows path segment such as \001 (every t.TempDir there) or \2024 reads as an octal string escape, and with any credential held the kit runs out of decode budget on the whole 78 KB description and withholds it, so agent-context printed only the kit's notice. Windows accepts forward slashes. A reprint regenerates agent_context.go and would drop the call.

handfixes.summary: a row the credential kit withholds from the store is skipped and named; the rest of the batch is stored and sync keeps walking, then ends that resource failed with the row ids
handfixes.why: One withheld row aborted the whole batch transaction, and sync returned on it, so a single large ordinary record (or one that really carried a held credential) stopped the resource and every row after it was never synced (#612, hubspot-calls-crm). The row is still withheld; it is now named in a sync_error event and in the resource's error, the run exits non-zero, and the watermark stays so the next run fetches it again. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe withheld-rows).

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.

retired.reason: tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0 builds a per-command blocked set (blockedDestinationFlags, blockedInputFlags, root control-plane flags), removes those flags from each tool's schema, refuses any undeclared argument name (so "db=/path" is refused) and skips '=' names in cliArgsFromMCP.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Upstreamed as cli-printing-press #4647: every value-carrying branch of cliArgsFromMCP joins the value to its flag (--k=v, one element per list item), and the press generates TestCliArgsFromMCP_ValueCannotSmuggleBlockedFlag.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: The note paused HTTP mode until a reprint because the build served HTTP with no token. Press 4.34.0 HTTP mode refuses to start without <PREFIX>_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, answers 401 without the right bearer, binds 127.0.0.1 by default and refuses a non-loopback address without TLS; onboard.py now writes HTTP guidance that follows the binary (cc-skills #14) and never writes this note, so the entry would fail on every re-onboard.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0's cobratree mirror derives one blocked set per command (destination, input, mcp:write-flags, mcp:read-flags and root control-plane flags), leaves those flags out of the tool schema and refuses them, and any undeclared argument, by name.
